newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel sees further job cuts in '97,'98.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees further job cuts in '97,'98.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk said there would be further job cuts at the company in 1997 and early 1998, after 10,000 job losses in 1997, but he declined to speculate on the number.

He said the actual job cut decisions were made on a local level and discussed with European wide staff representation bodies -- a veiled reference to the outcry Renault invoked with its sudden decision to shut a plant in Belgium.
Tchuruk said that the group, looking at outsourcing for some of its components, could close a number of factories in Europe but would try to look for a buyer for the sites.
During 1996, Alcatel used 5.1 billion francs ($894 million) in restructuring provisions, leaving it with 10.5 billion for further restructuring in telecoms and cables.
In 1995, Alcatel shed 4,500 jobs and used 1.6 billion in restructuring provisions.
Tchuruk said that the level of provisions had proved to be "correct".
At the end of 1996, Alcatel had 190,000 staff.
